Public Meetings - November 23, 2026
1.
Public Meetings - 7:00 p.m.
K. Douglas, Supervisor, Legislative Services, advised that the Public Meetings are being held in a hybrid meeting format with members of the public attending both in person and virtually. Ms. Douglas stated that Members of Council would receive a summary of all submissions upon publication of the minutes of the Public Meetings. Ms. Douglas provided an overview of the format of the public meetings. She advised that members of the public who wish to be notified of the next report related to any of the public meetings or who wish to be placed on an Interested Parties List for a matter should email the Town's Planning and Development Department at
[email protected]
or call 905.430.4306.
1.
PDP 51-26, Planning and Development (Planning Services) Department Report
Re: Zoning By-law Amendment, Winchester LP, Winchester GP Inc., (c/o Weston Consulting), 114 Winchester Road E. & 7 Duke St., File No. DEV-26-26 (Z-11-26)
Ahasar Syed, Planner I, Development, provided a PowerPoint presentation which included an overview of the application.
Jacob Lapointe, representing Winchester LP, Winchester GP Inc., provided a PowerPoint presentation which included a detailed overview of the application.
The Chair indicated that comments would now be received by members of the public.
Crystal Pearce, Resident, raised concerns regarding traffic, parking, privacy, shadowing, construction impacts, and the design of the development. Ms. Pearce requested clarification regarding the timing of the traffic study, access to the development, and the construction timeline.
Chris Casola, Resident, raised concerns regarding traffic, speeding, and pedestrian safety. Mr. Casola requested clarification and validation of the traffic study and whether it accounted for construction in the area.
Jeff Dinsmore, Resident, raised concerns regarding traffic, speeding, parking, and noise impacts from the proposed commercial units. Mr. Dinsmore asked that the number of townhouse units be reduced and commercial units be removed. He further requested that a direct access point to Winchester Road be incorporated into the proposal.
Greg Scott, Resident, raised concerns regarding traffic, driving behaviour and collisions. Mr. Scott requested that a recently installed median on Winchester Road be removed.
Dennis Hayward, Resident, raised concerns regarding road infrastructure, traffic, and parking congestion.
Chris Braznick, Resident, raised concerns regarding the height of the townhouse units located on the northern property boundary abutting existing residential backyards.
Kyle Grant, Resident, raised concerns regarding density, pedestrian safety, snow storage, overflow event parking during the Brooklin Spring Fair, and vehicle headlights intruding into nearby homes.
Kent Lambie, Resident, raised concerns regarding privacy, the design being incompatible with the character of the area, traffic, and negative impacts on neighbouring property values.
Albert Ems, Resident, requested that the Region of Durham be consulted on the application given that Winchester Road is a Regional road.
There were no further submissions from the public.
2.
PDP 52-26, Planning and Development (Planning Services) Department Report
Re:  Draft Plan of Subdivision and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications, North Whitby Holdings Inc., 2656377 Ontario Inc., and 7510 Thickson Road Holdings Inc., 7510 and 7570 Thickson Road North, File No. DEV-31-26 (SW-2026-01, Z-12-26)
Brad Anderson, Principal Planner, Development, provided a PowerPoint presentation which included an overview of the applications.
Jack Wong and Ben McKillop, representing North Whitby Holdings Inc., 2656377 Ontario Inc., and 7510 Thickson Road Holdings Inc., provided a PowerPoint presentation which included a detailed overview of the application.
The Chair indicated that comments would now be received by members of the public.
Thomas Coughlan, Resident, raised concerns regarding impact to the wells on his property, habitat protection for at-risk species, stormwater runoff, road salt contamination, and grading impacts along Thickson Road.
There were no further submissions from the public.
The meeting adjourned at 8:14 p.m.
